newsitem.title: CHINA: China city looks to business to unblock toilets.
newsitem.headline: China city looks to business to unblock toilets.

text.p: A city in central China is flushing away socialist-style management of its public toilets in a bid to boost lavatorial standards.

Fuyang city in Anhui province had auctioned management contracts for 18 toilets, and delighted officials were already reporting dramatic improvements at the privately-run public conveniences, the Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.
"People wanting to spend a penny in China have been given the chance of a lifetime," it said. "Experts say this is the first auction for public toilets in China."
China's toilet revolutionaries have long complained of poor sanitation at many public toilets, which in many cities are a key source of relief for residents without indoor plumbing.

Toilet contractors in Fuyang would pay management fees to the local lavatory administration and would responsible for cleaning work, Xinhua said but gave no details of how much they would be allowed to charge users for their services.
